sections.text:
Aaron, peace be upon him, is the older brother of the Prophet Moses, peace be upon him. He was distinguished by his extreme eloquence, eloquence, calmness, and gentleness.

When God Almighty commissioned Moses on Mount Tur to go to Pharaoh, Moses realized the seriousness and difficulty of the task.

Because Moses was suffering from a tongue-tie (slurred speech due to an ember placed in his mouth as a child in Pharaoh’s palace to avoid his sword), he asked God for special help.

He called on Moses, saying: “And appoint for me a minister from my family, * Aaron, my brother, * strengthen my armor with him, * and involve him in my affairs.”

God answered Moses' prayer, and inspired Aaron to be a prophet, messenger, and minister to his brother in the greatest confrontation against the tyranny of Pharaoh.

Aaron was the strong support for his brother. Together they faced Pharaoh, endured his mockery and sarcasm, and were patient with the stubbornness of the children of Israel.

After surviving Pharaoh and drowning in the sea, Moses went to the appointed time of his Lord on Mount Tur to receive the Tablets (the Torah) for forty days.

Before he left, Moses appointed his brother Aaron as his successor over the Children of Israel, saying to him: “Register with me among my people and make peace, and do not follow the path of the corrupt.”

In Moses' absence, a hypocritical man called "the Samaritan" appeared. He took advantage of the ignorance and weakness of faith of the children of Israel and made a golden calf for them.

The Samaritan threw into the calf a handful of dirt from the hoof print of Gabriel’s horse, peace be upon him, and the calf began to emit a sound resembling bellowing when it entered the air.

The children of Israel were fascinated by this golden calf and began to worship it and walk around it, forgetting about God, who had just saved them from Pharaoh!
Aaron stood with all courage, warning them and forbidding them strongly, saying: “O my people, you have been tempted by it. Indeed, your Lord is the Most Merciful, so follow me and obey my command.”

But they did not listen to him, and they almost killed him because he was trying to prevent them from this great polytheism.

Aaron chose not to start a civil war between them until Moses returned to decide the matter firmly.

When Moses returned and saw his people worshiping the calf, he became very angry, threw the tablets out of his hand, and grabbed his brother Aaron’s head and beard, dragging him to him, agitated, blaming him.

Aaron said with gentleness and brotherly gentleness: “O son of my mother, do not take my beard or my head. I was afraid that you would say, ‘You have divided the Children of Israel,’ and you did not heed my words.”

Moses calmed down when he realized that Aaron had done nothing wrong, and that the blame fell on the Samaritan and on the ignorance of the children of Israel.

Moses prayed to his Lord: “My Lord, forgive me and my brother and admit us into Your mercy, and You are the Most Merciful of those who show mercy.”

The Samaritan was exiled, the golden calf was burned and blown up in the sea, and the children of Israel returned to monotheism after arduous repentance.

Aaron continued to support his brother Moses at all stations, even when God commanded them to enter the Holy Land and the children of Israel refused and became cowardly, Aaron stood steadfastly with Moses.

Aaron, peace be upon him, died shortly before Moses in the Sinai Desert, and Moses mourned him deeply for the loss of his brother, his companion, and his faithful friend.
The lesson of Aaron's story is the importance of a good friend and brother in supporting a person in his life's tasks, and that brotherhood in God is the greatest bond of strength.
